consumers are willing to pay a premium for information on meat labels and that the information they seek is nutrition and ingredient information.
consumers are more concerned with nutritional and ingredient information on the labels, and this information helps them to select beef and other meats.
consumers are interested in meat labels and that nutrition and ingredient labels are positively related with meat purchases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of meat labels in influencing consumer meat consumption pattern.
the influence of different meat labels on consumer attitude and meat purchase and consumption.
the role of meat labels in consumer decision making, and how the information on meat labels affects meat consumption pattern.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consumers’ attitudes towards food labels and their consumption patterns are influenced by different aspects of food labels.
the information on meat labels helps consumers select the meat products they consume, but the level of detail on the labels is not always sufficient.
the information on meat labels is very important and helps consumers in the purchase of meat products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers’ attitude towards meat labels was generally positive and that nutrition and ingredient labels were the most important information that consumers wanted on meat labels.
the information on meat labels has a significant influence on meat consumption pattern.

the consumers want more nutrition and ingredient information, which is consistent with the findings in other food categories (e.g., dairy products).
